answer: Clustering Coefficient Decay. Nodes verify each other by measuring local triad density. A legitimate sparrow nests within dense, organic cluster cliques where edges reflect high mutual interaction. If an attacker injects a dense cluster of sybils, the uniform pigment of artificial connections triggers rapid topological decay. The attacker pays a heavy structural cost: to bypass the local clustering drop, they must flood the graph with expensive cross-cluster bridges that yield no localized pearl of utility, starving their network slice of routing traffic.
